title: Spacing and a withheld position test the spatial inverse
advisorGate: S4A accepted; S4B proposed cases approved 2026-09-27
question: When does a second spatial sample add stable information, and can a withheld sample expose phase drift?
model: M(x)=[exp(-ikx),exp(ikx)]; singular values sqrt(2±2|cos(kDelta)|); norm-bounded noise eta U_min gives coefficient error eta/sigma_min

units.response: normalized complex amplitude in arbitrary reference units
units.eta: total complex observation L2 norm, not per-channel bound

controls: Rank-deficient zero/half-wavelength endpoints with explicit kernel
Worst-direction bounded noise at four full-rank separations
Second-only phase drift fits two channels but predicts third incorrectly
Common global phase rotation is consistent
limits: One-dimensional known-c model and common phase reference assumed
Half-wavelength singular cases are not inverted
A third sample can reject this mismatch but cannot certify every physical assumption
Noise direction is constructed worst case; not a phone error distribution
incomingEvidence: S4A ideal quarter-wave inversion succeeded, but actual positions/phase/noise determine whether its extra channel is informative.
